Neither source states nor immediately implies the all-order unique-zero crossing with explicit switching-time brackets or the exact moving sharp-gradient norm maximizer. Chinta et al. covers the heat Gaussian model without this shape classification; distinct relevant published-record searches returned no stronger covering claim. Residual priority risk remains unindexed equivalent work.

value.rationale: The exact maximizing spatial site of a discrete heat gradient is a natural sharp Fourier/semigroup invariant. Classifying every change at all times is qualitatively stronger than a finite Bessel table, numerical mode tracking, or generic Gaussian approximation. The strict quadratic interval enclosure gives explicit, computable barriers for all phase transitions and the exact ℓ¹→ℓ∞ gradient norm follows. This clarifies the discrete shift of the gradient peak as heat diffuses, with potential in lattice gradient estimates and spatial kernel sampling.
